comparisons.peer_topic: Largest non-U.S. country exposures by location
comparisons.peer_summary: The United Kingdom was the largest non-U.S. country exposure at $62.0 billion (up $6.1 billion) and Germany was the second largest at $37.0 billion (up $1.4 billion) as of December 31, 2024, with increases primarily due to higher central bank deposits.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures involve the impact of external factors on cash positions with central banks. Citi places excess liquidity with the Central Bank of Russia due to specific sanctions restrictions preventing reverse repos. BAC reports that its largest non-U.S. country exposures (UK and Germany) increased primarily due to 'higher deposits with the central bank,' though the driver was not explicitly stated as sanctions-related restrictions on other instruments, but rather general exposure growth.

sentences.text: Due to sanctions restrictions, as well as Citi being unable to enter into reverse repos beginning in the third quarter of 2024, any excess liquidity is placed with the Central Bank of Russia.

Our largest non-U.S. country exposure at December 31, 2024 was the United Kingdom with net exposure of $62.0 billion, which increased $6.1 billion from December 31, 2023 primarily due to higher deposits with the central bank.

Our second largest non-U.S. country exposure was Germany with net exposure of $37.0 billion at December 31, 2024, which increased $1.4 billion from December 31, 2023 primarily due to higher deposits with the central bank.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm continues to monitor its exposure to Russia, which consists of cash placed with the central bank excluding client deposits, and currently believes this remaining exposure is not material. Information regarding Russian litigation is referenced in Note 30.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan disclose that cash placements with the Central Bank of Russia constitute their remaining Russia exposure, explicitly excluding client deposits. Citi provides context on the operational constraint (inability to enter reverse repos since Q3 2024) driving these placements, whereas JPMorgan characterizes this remaining exposure as 'not material' without detailing the specific transactional restrictions imposed on the funds.

sentences.text: (2) Cash on deposit and placements are primarily with the Central Bank of Russia.
Due to sanctions restrictions, as well as Citi being unable to enter into reverse repos beginning in the third quarter of 2024, any excess liquidity is placed with the Central Bank of Russia.

The Firm continues to monitor its exposure to Russia, which corresponds to cash placed with the central bank, but which excludes deposits placed on behalf of clients at the Deposit Insurance Agency of Russia.
The Firm currently believes that its remaining exposure to Russia is not material.

comparisons.peer_summary: Increases in exposure to Germany and Japan compared to December 31, 2023, were driven by cash placed with their respective central banks, predominantly due to client-driven market-making activities and higher client deposits for Germany.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the management of excess liquidity and cash placements with central banks. Citi explains that sanctions forced excess liquidity into the Central Bank of Russia. JPMorgan highlights that increases in exposure to Germany and Japan were similarly driven by 'cash placed with the central bank' resulting from client-driven market-making activities, illustrating a shared operational mechanic of holding central bank deposits for liquidity management in key jurisdictions.
